name: MathlibAnnex.EquivalentSeminorm.IsContraction
title: Continuous linear maps bounded by a seminorm

content.display_title: Continuous linear maps bounded by a seminorm
content.one_sentence_role: Defines the pointwise contraction condition relative to a stored equivalent seminorm.
content.natural_language_statement: Let $X,Y$ be real normed spaces and let $p$ be the seminorm of an equivalent-seminorm datum on $X$, with stored constants $c,C>0$ satisfying $c\|x\|\le p(x)\le C\|x\|$ for every $x\in X$ and with $p$ continuous. A continuous real-linear map $A:X\to Y$ is a contraction relative to this datum exactly when $\|Ax\|\le p(x)$ for every $x\in X$.
content.definition_explanation:
For the given continuous linear map $A$, define

$$\operatorname{IsContraction}_p(A)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\forall x\in X,\ \|Ax\|\le p(x).$$

Here $p$ is evaluated on the domain vector, and the norm is the codomain norm.
content.assumptions: The map $A$ is already continuous and real-linear. The domain carries its reference norm and an equivalent-seminorm datum $p$ with positive comparison constants and continuity. The codomain $Y$ is any real normed space, with the norm appearing on the left of the inequality. No dimension, completeness or bijectivity condition is imposed.
content.conclusion: The declaration defines a proposition about the given map $A$. The separately defined contraction set is precisely $\{A:X\to Y\text{ continuous and real-linear}:\ \forall x,\ \|Ax\|\le p(x)\}$.
content.lean_realization_notes: When a later application takes $Y=\mathbb R^N$ in the form of real functions on a finite index set, its default norm is the supremum norm. This is a specialization of the same predicate. The definition itself supplies neither an operator nor an inverse.
